title.narrative: Support to formalize the Housing, Land, and Property (HLP) rights of minorities in Sinjar (phase II).

description.narrative:
The proposed project is phase II of the previously implemented project “Support to Housing, Land and Property Rights for IDPs in Nineveh” and it is related to the implementation of the Legal Decree approved by the Council of Ministers of Iraq on December 2022 to officially recognize minority HLP rights in Sinjar.
The goal of the project is to contribute to peace and stabilization in Iraq by formalizing the HLP rights of minorities and resolving discriminatory practices against minorities in Sinjar.
The objective of the project is “Informed, voluntary, and sustainable returns to Sinjar for minorities and vulnerable displaced populations as a durable solution are supported and facilitated through formalized HLP rights”.
To achieve this objective, the project aims to:
(a) Support HLP rights of displaced persons from minorities by providing legal assistance to formalize their HLP rights and obtain ownership title deeds. (b) Enhance the capacity of the national and local government by providing training to efficiently manage the overall process of formalization.
The project is expected to support the formalization of HLP rights and the peaceful reintegration of 36,000 internally displaced people (IDPs)/returnees including women and youth (including orphans) to their areas of origin.
Based on the (Phase I) previously implemented project, a multi-pronged approach will be taken in this project to support the HLP rights of IDPs and returnees from minority groups. In the process of formalizing HLP rights for IDPs and returnees, the proposed project will also contribute to the overall goal of complementary and joint efforts with other partners, projects, and programmes to multiply the impact on other components related to the digital registration of HLP rights by creating a legal background for the ICT-based solution, assisting in the digitization phase, automating the property registration systems, conducting study visits, and supporting capacity-building on cadasters aiming to digitize property records, and developing the issuance of digital title deeds with a new GIS system, improving land governance, and improving the overall living conditions of Iraqis, including IDPs and returnees.
